A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WM/LMC study. Their complete main texts and appendices A–H are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original model-merging experiments, singular-vector analyses and sensitivity studies, including results on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and ImageNet.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports WM optimization curves and adjusted output-layer singular-value distributions.

M1.justification: The WM, AM and STE objectives and permutation-search procedures remain unchanged. The added output-layer rescaling is a diagnostic analysis, not a newly introduced component of the merging method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and ImageNet, including the existing two-model and three-model comparisons. The new diagnostics reuse existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same WM, AM, STE and unpermuted comparisons. The revised Guerrero-Peña attribution refers to the same Sinkhorn method; newly cited related work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols monitor WM across optimization epochs, including a VGG11 trajectory beyond ten epochs, and compare spectra after output-layer rescaling (Figures 6 and 8). Appendix D's main training and permutation-search settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H.1 adds learning curves examining WM convergence and the ten-epoch stopping choice. Appendix H.2 adds a rescaling check supporting v4's existing explanation of output-layer spectral differences. Existing width, regularization, threshold and ImageNet analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 adds a t-test at the 5% significance level for Taylor-versus-observed barrier differences. Appendix H.7 changes the three-model trial description from five to three, reconciling v4's appendix with its Section 6.3; this does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds barrier-difference results, including MNIST's 0.069 ± 0.028, and removes test-accuracy entries. Section 3.2 now reports significant discrepancies for all datasets instead of excepting MNIST. Figures 6 and 8 add diagnostic findings; retained benchmark and three-model scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 strengthens the loss-function assumption from twice differentiable to class C3, providing stronger regularity for the stated cubic Taylor remainder. The other theorems, mathematical definitions and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion qualify the claimed equivalence of AM's and WM's mechanisms from 'the same' to 'likely the same.' The principal WM alignment explanation and three-model comparison claims are retained.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly acknowledges that the individual-layer analysis does not fully explain multilayer-network behavior. Section 3.2 also qualifies the midpoint-barrier rationale by discussing how unequal generalization can shift the maximum. Existing width and ImageNet limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 identifies PyTorch's vhp function for Hessian-vector products, replacing a generic computational description. Conversely, the FFCV reference drops commit identifier 4dd291. Appendix D otherwise retains the hardware, software versions, hyperparameters and principal implementation links.

R1.justification: v5 adds Adilova et al. (2024) on barrier location and distinguishes its permutation analysis from Singh et al. (2024) on Taylor approximations and Yunis et al. (2024) on spectral training dynamics. These are limited extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and several explanations receive localized edits, Appendix D corrects the expansion of LMC, affiliations are updated, and ethics/reproducibility statements are added. The main narrative structure and most appendix exposition are preserved.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figures 6 and 8, revises Table 1's columns and significance highlighting, and creates main-text Table 3 from existing appendix results. v4's accuracy-landscape Figure 6 becomes an enlarged, two-row appendix Figure 17. Other displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves rigor through the stronger Theorem 3.1 assumption, significance testing, convergence/scaling checks and consistent trial reporting. Qualifying the AM claim and acknowledging the unresolved multilayer gap improve scientific precision. These gains outweigh the limited reporting losses from removing Table 1 accuracies and the FFCV commit identifier; the central evidence otherwise remains largely unchanged.
